Daily Digest Saturday, August 29, 2026

Enterprise Software Up 13%, But AI's Winners and Losers Are Diverging Fast

Enterprise software grows but AI reshapes categories unevenly. AWS launches managed web search for agents. GEO becomes essential B2B strategy.

  1. 1

    IDC: Enterprise Software Grows 13%, But AI Impact Remains Uneven

    New IDC research shows the global enterprise application market grew 13% by mid-2026 — but AI isn't lifting all boats equally. Workflow automation software (Atlassian +28%, ServiceNow +24%) is surging while customer service and HCM categories stall. Sprinklr grew just 6.8% last quarter. The insight: AI is being repriced, not replaced. Usage-based models are cannibalizing seat licenses faster than new AI revenue appears.

    Read on Cyprus Mail ↗
  2. 2

    AWS Web Search Goes GA for Bedrock AgentCore

    AWS pushed Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to general availability — a managed server-side tool that lets agents fetch live, cited web knowledge without data leaving the customer's AWS account. Initially available in US East (N. Virginia). This is AWS making a play to be the secure default for enterprise agent deployments.

    Read on AI Agent Store ↗
  3. 3

    GEO Agencies Ranked: First Page Sage Leads B2B Optimization

    First Page Sage analyzed 54 agencies offering Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) services and ranked the top 8 for B2B. The practice of optimizing for AI-generated recommendations — appearing in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini responses — is becoming essential as B2B buyers increasingly vet vendors through AI chatbots. SAP client Omniscient Digital made the list.

    Read on First Page Sage ↗
  4. 4

    Monetate Acquires Simon AI for Real-Time Personalization

    Monetate acquired Simon AI to connect website personalization tools with unified customer data across digital channels. AI agents now analyze real-time inventory updates, weather data, and customer interaction histories to select product recommendations. The CDP-to-personalization pipeline just got shorter.

    Read on MarTech ↗
  5. 5

    Aziro Launches Aziron: Enterprise Agent Execution Platform

    New startup Aziro launched Aziron, an enterprise agent execution platform that brings agents, workflows, documents, models and enterprise tools together in a single governed environment. The pitch: move from AI-generated answers to completed, auditable work. Governance-first agent platforms are having a moment. Read this one: The IDC piece on uneven AI impact. The story isn't "AI is transforming enterprise software" — it's "AI is transforming some categories while others scramble to reprice." Workflow automation is winning. Customer service and HCM are vulnerable. That divergence matters for PMMs positioning products in either camp.
